item.title: The New AI Superpowers: Focus and Followthrough [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: The article discusses how AI's ability to accelerate task completion paradoxically contributes to burnout by enabling people to start many projects simultaneously without finishing them. The author reflects on personal experience, noting that despite AI increasing productivity, the finite nature of human time and energy means that spreading oneself too thin leads to exhaustion rather than relief. The author advocates for a strategy of focusing deeply on fewer projects and following through thoroughly, rather than expanding the number of tasks. Drawing on concepts from essentialism and the analogy of a total versus partial eclipse, the article emphasizes the value of dedicating effort to achieve high-quality outcomes. The piece concludes that AI should be used to save time and enhance focus, helping people avoid burnout and produce more meaningful work.

item.title: Researchers develop hybrid probabilistic forecasting system combining time series and NLP to predict roadblocks in Bolivia, improving accuracy over traditional models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Roadblocks in Bolivia cause significant economic losses estimated at 4% of GDP, yet local predictive systems have been lacking. This study presents a hybrid forecasting system that integrates time series decomposition with natural language processing of six years of Bolivian news to detect early signals of social tension leading to roadblocks. The system was tested over 1,762 days across seven forecasting horizons and outperformed statistical models like SARIMA and LightGBM, achieving an AUC-ROC of 0.677 at the shortest horizon and reducing prediction error significantly. The methodology uses vector semantic embeddings and zero-shot classification to capture discursive escalation before roadblocks occur. Validation showed consistent error reduction across all horizons, demonstrating that incorporating semantic news signals can detect social tension peaks missed by historical data alone. This approach offers a technical tool for risk management in critical transport corridors affected by social conflicts in Bolivia.

item.title: LeAct introduces a method to recover natural-language reasoning from expert system actions, improving AI reasoning across games and robotics benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: LeAct (Learning to reason from Actions) is a new approach that extracts latent chains of thought from expert systems, which typically produce optimal actions without explaining their reasoning. By sampling candidate reasoning paths and selecting those that improve action recovery, LeAct enables AI models to learn from expert actions and generalize beyond them. The method achieves near-optimal performance on small games, outperforms expert-iteration baselines by five times on larger scales, and improves training on a robotics benchmark where direct imitation falls short. This framework positions expert systems as a novel source of reasoning supervision for foundation models.

item.title: MetaEvolve framework trains LLMs to develop self-evolution meta-skills via reinforcement learning on coding tasks, improving performance by up to 46.9% on out-of-distribution benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers present MetaEvolve, a framework that cultivates meta-skills like self-reflection and iterative refinement in large language models through a data synthesis pipeline, evolution-aware reinforcement learning, and evolutionary search at inference time. The approach leverages program execution as a continuous reward signal to train models on large-scale code data, aiming to generalize these skills beyond coding to open-ended problems. MetaEvolve was evaluated across seven coding benchmarks, outperforming the strongest baseline by 10.01% on in-distribution tasks and 24.12% on out-of-distribution tasks. It also achieved a 46.9% relative improvement on algorithm optimization problems outside the training domain, demonstrating that explicitly training self-evolution meta-skills can enhance AI autonomy and capability.

item.title: Researchers present DBA-Bench, a production-fidelity benchmark for evaluating LLM-based database operations agents across 106 scenarios with PostgreSQL environments [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers introduce DBA-Bench, a benchmark designed to address gaps in evaluating large language model (LLM)-based database agents by simulating production-like environments with multi-turn interactions, complex observations, and multiple remediation options. The benchmark includes 106 scenarios across seven task domains using instrumented PostgreSQL setups with active workloads and persistent states, defining success by measurable recovery or fault elimination under safety constraints. The study evaluates nine baseline groups, including foundation models, GPT-5.5-backed agents, and a human database administrator (DBA) reference, across 848 automated runs. Results show automated agents achieve Diagnosis, Outcome, and Safe Pass rates of 32.7%, 19.6%, and 12.4%, respectively, with the best automated Safe Pass rate at 17.9% compared to 93.4% for the human DBA. Performance declines on harder scenarios, highlighting challenges in safe end-to-end remediation by automated systems.

item.title: Researchers introduce Byte-Prefix Marginalization for cross-tokenizer on-policy distillation, improving student model training across multiple benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers propose Byte-Prefix Marginalization (BPM), a method that re-expresses a teacher language model's next-token distribution over a student model's vocabulary in a shared byte space, preserving probability mass and aligning tokenization. BPM assigns teacher token probabilities to the longest student token whose byte representation prefixes the teacher token's bytes, aggregating mass and handling unmatched mass explicitly, enabling vocabulary-complete and mass-preserving targets for on-policy distillation without requiring shared tokenizers. Evaluated on models including Qwen3-32B, GLM-Z1-9B-0414, and MiniMax-M2.7, BPM outperforms existing cross-tokenizer methods on six mathematics and programming benchmarks, improving average scores by 3.7 to 6.6 points over the strongest baselines.

item.title: Researchers use Jungian Cognitive Functions for activation steering to control personality traits in Llama-3.1-8B, revealing geometric relationships in transformer layers [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers propose a framework using the eight Jungian Cognitive Functions to represent and control personality in large language models (LLMs) through activation steering, moving beyond static trait models like the Big Five. They introduce a Jungian evaluation protocol and a dataset of over 2,100 role-playing character narrations to test this approach on Llama-3.1-8B, demonstrating effective monotonic control over all eight cognitive functions. Their analysis shows that personality information is concentrated in the middle transformer layers, steering vectors reflect structured geometric relationships aligned with rational and irrational function distinctions, and multi-dimensional steering directions cannot be formed by linear combinations of single-function directions. These findings offer new insights into personality representation in LLM activation space and establish a framework for interpretable and multi-dimensional personality control.

item.title: Researchers propose SPRO framework for process reinforcement learning that derives intrinsic process rewards and redefines step-wise advantage, improving training efficiency and accuracy without extra computational cost [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers introduce Self-Guided Process Reward Optimization (SPRO), a novel framework for process reinforcement learning that derives process rewards intrinsically from the policy model and redefines step-wise advantage using Cumulative Process Rewards and Masked Step Advantage. SPRO outperforms vanilla GRPO with 3.4 times higher training efficiency and a 12.9% improvement in test accuracy while maintaining stable policy entropy and reducing response length. The framework achieves these gains without additional computational overhead compared to existing outcome-supervised reinforcement learning methods, supporting its potential for industrial applications.

item.title: Researchers find that larger language models compound mistakes faster despite improved accuracy, revealing a self-perpetuating failure mode invisible to the models themselves [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A study analyzing three families of language models shows that as models scale, their knowledge gaps decrease but the rate of knowledge degradation and error compounding increases significantly. The researchers identify a causal mechanism where models commit to low-probability tokens and then condition subsequent outputs on these errors, leading to a snowball effect that persists even when the model's own uncertainty signals diminish. This failure mode evades self-monitoring tools and results in more frequent fabrications despite higher confidence levels. The findings highlight a trade-off between capability and reliability in larger language models and suggest that current approaches to improving model accuracy may overlook this inherent risk.

item.title: Researchers introduce DFAH-Bench to measure observable instability in financial AI agent decisions, analyzing over 4,700 episodes across synthetic compliance and financial DataOps groups [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: DFAH-Bench benchmarks the consistency of financial AI agents by assessing decision agreement and tool-path agreement during replay, highlighting variations in execution despite stable decisions. The study analyzed 4,157 retrospective episodes and 570 prospective episodes, revealing decision agreement rates above 94% but significant discrepancies in tool usage paths and argument-result trajectories. This approach aims to improve replay fidelity, investigation, and change control in AI-driven financial decision-making processes.

item.title: Report: Major companies resume hiring despite earlier predictions of widespread job losses due to AI
item.description: Major corporations are beginning to increase their hiring activities, countering earlier forecasts that artificial intelligence would lead to significant job cuts. This shift suggests that the impact of AI on employment may be more nuanced than initially expected. The trend reflects a reassessment of workforce needs as companies integrate AI technologies while continuing to expand their teams.

item.title: Researchers propose Adversarial Style Optimization to enhance visual jailbreak attacks on Multimodal Large Language Models by exploiting stylistic vulnerabilities using GRPO-based image editing [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: A recent study introduces Adversarial Style Optimization (ASO), a method that improves jailbreak attacks on Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) by targeting stylistic weaknesses rather than content. The researchers found that while MLLMs understand content across various visual styles, their safety mechanisms can be bypassed by specific stylistic triggers. ASO fine-tunes an image-editing model with a Group Relative Policy Optimization agent and a reward function combining refusal detection and semantic evaluation to optimize stylistic modifications on adversarial images. Experiments show that ASO significantly increases the success rate of state-of-the-art visual jailbreak attacks, revealing stylistic biases as a scalable vulnerability for testing MLLM security. The researchers have made the ASO code publicly available for further study and development.

item.title: Researchers probe latent Colombian identity and stereotypes in Qwen2.5-7B using Natural Language Autoencoders on Spanish and English prompts [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A pilot study investigates whether the large language model Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct internally encodes Colombian identity, socioeconomic status, or stereotypes when processing Colombian-Spanish and English prompts. The research uses Natural Language Autoencoders to analyze activations from a specific model layer across 30 prompts with explicit, implicit, and neutral Colombian cues. The study offers descriptive and qualitative insights into latent nationality and stereotype representations within the model before these appear in its outputs, contributing to understanding bias and interpretability in language models for underrepresented Spanish dialects.

item.title: Researchers introduce Khondo, a bilingual multimodal benchmark for splitting Bangladeshi government form packets, highlighting challenges in page-order reconstruction [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Khondo, the first benchmark dataset for splitting document packets of Bangladeshi government forms that operates directly on bilingual (Bangla-English) page images. The dataset covers five concatenation schemes across 14 administrative domains with annotated boundaries and page orders, enabling evaluation of document clustering and page ordering tasks. Evaluations show models can cluster pages into original documents but struggle to restore correct page order, especially when pages are shuffled. The study identifies page-order reconstruction as a key challenge in vision-based document understanding for low-resource languages and provides Khondo as a resource to advance research in this area.

item.title: Researchers find data quality more critical than LoRA adapter capacity for closed-book QA in 4-bit Gemma-4-e4b models [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers studied embedding documents directly into the weights of a 4-bit Gemma-4-e4b model using LoRA adapters to enable closed-book question answering without retrieval or context-window limits. Their experiments across corpus sizes showed that once adapter capacity is sufficient, training data quality has a greater impact on accuracy than LoRA rank, learning rate, or architecture changes. They improved accuracy significantly by refining answer curation and confirmed that adapter capacity must scale with corpus size, noting interactions between rank and learning rate.

item.title: Researchers introduce J-CoT, a recurrent reasoning framework using vocabulary-indexed J-space to improve language model reasoning without full verbalization of intermediate steps [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed J-CoT, a new reasoning framework that operates within a vocabulary-indexed coordinate system called J-space to carry intermediate reasoning states as J-thoughts. This approach avoids the need for fully verbalized intermediate rationales and does not require recurrence over the entire hidden state, enabling more efficient reasoning in language models. Evaluations show that J-CoT-Zero matches or surpasses existing latent-reasoning baselines, while J-CoT-Train achieves top scores across mathematical, scientific, coding, and structured path-reasoning benchmarks.

item.title: Study benchmarks fine-tuning and retrieval strategies for Gemma 4 31B multimodal model on NRC Reactor Operator licensing exams, achieving near 80% accuracy on 8 of 14 tests [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: A recent study evaluated the 31-billion-parameter multimodal language model Gemma 4 31B-IT on the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission Reactor Operator licensing examination, benchmarking eight configurations combining fine-tuning and retrieval strategies. The fine-tuned model with fixed-size chunking retrieval met the human passing criterion on 8 out of 14 exams, reaching an aggregate accuracy close to 80%. No configuration without fine-tuning passed any exam. The research compared supervised fine-tuning with chain-of-thought rationales, retrieval-augmented generation using domain-specific documents, and retrieval-augmented fine-tuning, also analyzing fixed-size sliding-window chunking versus structure-aware chunking. Results showed that chunking strategy effectiveness depends on the model's training state, and retrieval-augmented fine-tuning underperformed standard fine-tuning. These findings inform effective integration of large language models into nuclear industry applications requiring specialized knowledge.

item.title: Researchers propose FSE model combining fast and slow experts to improve continual learning for named entity recognition, achieving state-of-the-art results on OntoNotes and FewNERD datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: The FSE (Fast-Slow Experts) model addresses challenges in continual learning for named entity recognition by using a fast expert to filter unlikely token spans and a slow expert to classify remaining spans, reducing catastrophic forgetting and enhancing knowledge sharing. A length-decay negative sampling strategy is also introduced to mitigate span imbalance. Experiments demonstrate that FSE achieves faster convergence and improved performance compared to existing methods on benchmark datasets.

item.title: MEUSLI launches open-source multilingual projector linking Whisper encoders with large language models for end-to-end ASR in 28 European languages [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: MEUSLI is an open-source multilingual projector that connects Whisper speech encoders with multilingual large language models, enabling end-to-end automatic speech recognition (ASR) across 28 European languages. It supports both high- and low-resource languages and can be extended to additional languages through continual learning techniques. Beyond ASR, MEUSLI also enables multilingual speech translation and topic identification with minimal task-specific training, providing a scalable foundation for diverse multilingual speech understanding applications.

item.title: Researchers introduce a multilayer taxonomy of 14 capability domains and 91 subskills for large language models, analyzing 15,934 papers from 2023 to 2025 to map research focus areas [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a multilayer taxonomy to classify large language model (LLM) capabilities into 14 domains and 91 subskills, moving beyond isolated task evaluations to structured capability analysis. They applied this taxonomy to 15,934 LLM-focused papers from major AI conferences between 2023 and 2025, revealing concentrated research on Language-Semantic Competence, Reasoning, Planning and Decision-Making, and Perception, while several domains received minimal attention. This taxonomy, guided by human cognitive science rather than LLM architecture, aims to improve research organization, identify coverage gaps, and support evaluation and training strategies by shifting the focus from tasks to capabilities.

item.title: Researchers analyze when large language models align with or diverge from human creativity evaluations, finding differences in sensitivity to novelty and contextual information [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers conducted three studies using six widely used large language models (LLMs) to examine how their creativity evaluations compare to human judgments. They found that LLMs generally rely on a narrower set of creativity standards, aligning most closely with humans on novelty but diverging on contextual factors like social and market information. Each LLM applied distinct evaluation standards, affecting their creativity judgments. The studies showed that LLM evaluations moderately correlated with human ratings, with models using broader standards better distinguishing more creative ideas. However, LLMs were less sensitive to contextual information that significantly influenced human creativity assessments. These findings suggest that alignment between LLM and human creativity evaluations depends on the type of evidence considered and the specific standards each model uses, making the choice of LLM evaluator important for recognizing creative ideas.

item.title: Survey finds organizations lack systematic processes to validate EU AI Act requirements in requirements engineering; experts see promise and risks in LLM-based validation tools [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: A study involving expert interviews and surveys reveals that many organizations developing or operating AI systems are unprepared to translate EU AI Act obligations into testable, auditable requirements and verifiable evidence. While the Act is considered highly relevant, structured mechanisms for capturing regulatory obligations, updating projects, and maintaining traceability are often missing. Participants from requirements engineering, data science, development, and compliance roles view large language model-based agentic validation tools as promising for mapping obligations to requirements and organizing evidence but express concerns about full automation and emphasize the need for safeguards. The study outlines minimum requirements for a closed-loop approach to meet EU AI Act compliance.

item.title: Researchers identify the Hard Decision Layer in transformers where answer rankings stabilize abruptly during inference, improving accuracy across multiple language models and datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers investigated how transformer-based language models commit to predictions in multiple-choice question answering and identified a Hard Decision Layer (HDL), a natural architectural feature where answer rankings stabilize abruptly during inference. This phenomenon was consistently observed across four language models-Qwen, Llama, Granite, and Mistral-and four benchmark datasets, without requiring learned routing policies or being affected by fine-tuning. The HDL corresponds with significant accuracy improvements, such as a 0.61 increase for Qwen on CommonsenseQA, after which performance stabilizes. Systematic tests confirmed that the HDL is a fundamental property of transformer architecture. These findings provide mechanistic insights into transformer inference and suggest potential for more efficient reasoning and model steering.

item.title: Researchers introduce FaithC4 benchmark to evaluate transcription faithfulness of vision-language models versus traditional OCR across English, Chinese, and Korean documents [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have found that vision-language models (VLMs) used for document understanding often rewrite imperfect text into more plausible forms rather than transcribing faithfully, a behavior undetected by standard OCR benchmarks. They introduced FaithC4, a multilingual benchmark with 1,455 single-page documents in English, Chinese, and Korean, containing three types of text perturbations to test transcription accuracy across 15 systems including general-purpose VLMs, OCR-specialized VLMs, and traditional OCR pipelines. The study revealed that general-purpose VLMs experience up to 4.5 points degradation in word error rate under perturbations, OCR-specialized VLMs degrade by 0.2 to 2 points, and traditional OCR pipelines degrade less than 0.6 points on English documents. Analysis of the Qwen3-VL-4B model showed that rewriting occurs when the model's internal representation of a perturbed word remains close to the original, while significant divergence leads to faithful transcription. Additionally, shorter words (4-6 characters) are rewritten up to 10% of the time, with rewriting dropping sharply for words longer than eight characters.

item.title: NVIDIA releases Molt, a PyTorch-native training framework for agentic reinforcement learning with asynchronous multimodal policy training [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: NVIDIA has introduced Molt, a scalable PyTorch-native training framework designed to simplify agentic reinforcement learning research by reducing the complexity of algorithm modifications and pipeline changes. Molt features a compact, clean codebase that allows researchers and AI coding assistants to trace and modify algorithm flows end to end, supporting asynchronous training of multimodal and mixture-of-experts policies without training on tokens not generated by the model itself. The framework achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art Megatron-based stacks under fully asynchronous protocols and is available as open source with recipes and containers on GitHub.

item.title: Researchers find causal evidence sets outperform attention-based training for sparse attention routing in language models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers tested the assumption that attention patterns reveal the context a model uses by comparing attention with causal dependence on retrieval tasks where evidence is known. They found that attention often disagrees with causal dependence, with models attending to outdated facts and varying attention across runs, leading to lower accuracy when training selectors on attention alone. Training selectors on causal evidence sets recovered by masking parts of the input improved accuracy significantly, matching or exceeding teacher model performance without requiring annotations. The study also observed similar conflicts in pretrained models, showing that attention indicates where a model looks but not necessarily what it depends on for answers.

item.title: Researchers introduce ADSD, a prompt-suffix attack that disrupts verifier acceptance in speculative decoding, increasing sample time by 62.3% on GSM8K while preserving task quality [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have identified a vulnerability in lossless acceleration schemes like speculative decoding, which rely on token-level alignment between draft and target models for faster inference. They introduced ADSD, the first prompt-suffix attack that collapses verifier acceptance by shifting draft probability toward tokens unlikely to be accepted by the target model, thereby undermining the alignment guarantee. ADSD employs Soft-Collapse, a surrogate aligned with the verifier's asymmetric acceptance rule, combined with a target-preservation objective to avoid obvious task corruption. The attack significantly increases mean sample time by 62.3% on the GSM8K dataset without degrading task performance. The study also demonstrates that this vulnerability spans multiple domains, speculative decoding methods, and model architectures, highlighting a broad operational risk in current acceleration techniques.

item.title: Researchers introduce MissionBench to evaluate zero-shot performance of aerial multimodal large language models on 120 mission-level tasks in 3D environments [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed MissionBench, a benchmark designed to assess the ability of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to perform long-horizon embodied tasks in aerial 3D environments using only egocentric observations and action history without fine-tuning. The benchmark includes 120 missions across five simulated environments and four task families, requiring agents to autonomously plan, navigate, and report outcomes from a single high-level instruction. Evaluation of 22 open- and closed-source MLLMs showed the best model succeeded in fewer than 35% of missions, compared to 84.4% human performance, highlighting the challenge of multi-step embodied tasks.

item.title: Study finds small vision-language models internally detect errors better than their verbalized confidence under image degradation but fail under severe low-light conditions [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers evaluated two small open-weight vision-language models, Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct and SmolVLM-Instruct, across six types of realistic image degradations at varying severity levels to compare their verbalized confidence against internal token probability as measures of uncertainty. They found that while the models' verbalized confidence was often constant or unavailable and poorly correlated with actual errors, the internal token probability reliably distinguished correct from incorrect answers except under severe underexposure where accuracy and error detection collapsed. The study concludes that these models possess usable self-knowledge not expressed in their verbal output, making internal probability a better signal for deferral decisions in constrained deployments, though neither confidence measure is reliable in extreme low-light scenarios.

item.title: Nanbeige4.2-3B launches as a compact 3B-parameter agentic model outperforming larger models on diverse benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Nanbeige4.2-3B is a compact general agentic model with 3 billion non-embedding parameters that delivers strong performance on code-agent, office-agent, and complex tool-use tasks while maintaining competitive reasoning in mathematics, coding, and science. It is pretrained from scratch on 28 trillion tokens using a Looped Transformer architecture that increases capacity without adding parameters. The model's training pipeline includes mixed-mode reinforcement learning with human feedback and agentic reinforcement learning to improve quality and stability. Evaluations show Nanbeige4.2-3B outperforms larger models such as Qwen3.5-9B and Gemma4-12B across various agentic benchmarks and remains competitive on reasoning and alignment tasks. Its performance with OpenClaw supports its use as a compact local personal assistant.

item.title: Researchers find LLMs' validation of pseudo-science varies widely by deployment configuration, with Grok showing inconsistent credibility scores across interfaces and updates [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A study tested four major large language models (Claude, Grok, GPT, Gemini) on their evaluation of ethnonationalist pseudo-science claims over several months, revealing significant variability in credibility scores depending on deployment settings. Grok's Fast versions assigned much higher credibility than others, and silent updates and interface differences caused drastic changes in outputs without public disclosure. The study highlights that an LLM's epistemic stance is not inherent but shaped by system prompts, safety layers, and deployment choices, which remain opaque to users and researchers. The authors call for new forms of epistemic accountability to address this public concern.

item.title: Researchers evaluate nine LLMs in morally charged social dilemmas, finding inconsistent moral behavior influenced by game structure and framing [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers introduced a framework to assess how large language models (LLMs) behave in social dilemmas where ethical considerations conflict with profit incentives, such as the prisoner's dilemma and public goods game. They tested nine models across varying moral contexts, opponent behaviors, and survival pressures, analyzing both behavior and reasoning to understand motives behind decisions. The study found cooperation rates varied widely from 7.9% to 76.3%, with no model consistently acting morally. Game structure and moral framing were the strongest factors affecting moral behavior, while reasoning traces revealed motives ranging from payoff-maximizing to moral and reputation-oriented. These findings highlight the situational fragility of current LLMs' ethical behavior and caution against deploying them where profit conflicts with ethical guidelines.

item.title: MedKGent framework uses LLM agents to build a temporally evolving medical knowledge graph from over 10 million PubMed abstracts, creating the largest LLM-derived medical KG to date [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: MedKGent is a Large Language Model agent framework designed to construct a medical knowledge graph that evolves over time by processing more than 10 million PubMed abstracts from 1975 to 2023. It employs two specialized agents: an Extractor Agent that identifies knowledge triples with confidence scores, and a Constructor Agent that integrates these triples into a temporal graph, reinforcing recurring information and resolving conflicts. The resulting knowledge graph contains 156,275 entities and nearly 3 million triples, with automated and expert evaluations showing about 90% validity for the extracted triples. In downstream tests, the MedKGent knowledge graph improved retrieval-augmented generation performance across five large language models on seven medical question-answering benchmarks. This positions MedKGent as a scalable and temporally aware infrastructure for representing medical knowledge and supporting AI research grounded in medical literature.

item.title: Researchers introduce InteractComp benchmark to evaluate search agents' ability to handle ambiguous queries through interaction, revealing low accuracy and stagnated interaction capabilities [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed InteractComp, a benchmark designed to test whether search agents can detect ambiguous user queries and actively interact to clarify them during search. The benchmark includes 210 expert-curated questions across nine domains that require interaction to resolve ambiguity. Evaluation of 17 models showed the best achieved only 13.73% accuracy on ambiguous queries, despite 71.50% accuracy with complete context, indicating overconfidence rather than reasoning flaws. The study found that forcing interaction significantly improved performance, demonstrating latent capabilities that current strategies fail to utilize. A longitudinal analysis revealed that while search performance improved seven-fold over 15 months, interaction abilities stagnated, highlighting a critical blind spot in search agent development. InteractComp offers a valuable resource for evaluating and training interactive capabilities in search agents, with code publicly available.

item.title: Researchers propose SwiftMem, a query-aware agentic memory system using temporal and semantic indexing to reduce retrieval latency for LLM agents [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: SwiftMem is designed to improve long-term context retrieval for large language model (LLM) agents by narrowing memory searches to query-relevant subsets using specialized temporal and semantic indexes. The system introduces a temporal index for efficient time-sensitive queries and a semantic DAG-Tag index that organizes topics hierarchically to map queries to relevant memory clusters. An embedding-tag co-consolidation mechanism addresses memory fragmentation by reorganizing storage based on semantic clusters to enhance locality. Evaluations on benchmarks like LoCoMo and LongMemEval show SwiftMem achieves search latencies around 10-13 milliseconds while maintaining competitive accuracy compared to existing HNSW-backed memory systems, offering an order-of-magnitude latency improvement on calibrated tests.

item.title: Researchers present WHBench, a benchmark evaluating 22 large language models on 47 women's health scenarios with expert validation, revealing no model exceeds 75% accuracy [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers developed the Women's Health Benchmark (WHBench), a suite of 47 expert-crafted scenarios across 10 women's health topics, to evaluate large language models (LLMs) on clinical accuracy, safety, equity, and guideline adherence. They assessed 22 models using a 23-criterion rubric and found that no model achieved more than 75 percent mean performance, with the best reaching 72.1 percent, highlighting significant gaps in fully correct responses and varying harm rates. The evaluation included 3,102 attempted responses and applied safety-weighted penalties and server-side score recalculations. Inter-rater reliability was moderate at the response label level but high for model ranking, supporting WHBench's utility for comparative evaluation. The benchmark aims to expose clinically meaningful failure modes such as outdated guidelines, unsafe omissions, dosing errors, and equity-related blind spots, emphasizing the need for expert oversight in clinical deployment and providing a public tool to track safer, more equitable progress in women's health AI.

item.title: Researchers present SURE-RAG, a selective retrieval-augmented generation method that verifies evidence sufficiency and uncertainty for multi-hop question answering, achieving high accuracy on HotpotQA-RAG v3 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: SURE-RAG is a new protocol designed to verify whether retrieved evidence sufficiently supports or refutes a candidate answer in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems. It aggregates local relation distributions between claims and passages into interpretable features to make a three-way decision on evidence sufficiency, improving answer reliability by answering only when support is established. The method was evaluated on the HotpotQA-RAG v3 benchmark using an artifact-aware protocol and outperformed baseline models and a GPT-4o judge while remaining fully auditable. The study also highlights that sufficiency verification differs from hallucination detection, as shown by contrasting SURE-RAG with GPT-4o on unsafe detection tasks.

item.title: Gemma 4 introduces open-weight multimodal language models with dense and Mixture-of-Experts architectures from 2.3B to 31B parameters, featuring improved encoders and a thinking mode for reasoning [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Gemma 4 is a new generation of open-weight, natively multimodal language models designed to enhance compute efficiency and reasoning capabilities. The model suite includes dense and Mixture-of-Experts architectures ranging from 2.3 billion to 31 billion parameters, with improved vision and audio encoders across all sizes and a unified, encoder-free architecture for the 12 billion parameter model that processes raw audio and image patches. It also integrates a thinking mode that allows the models to generate reasoning traces before responding. The design improvements in Gemma 4 enhance inference speed, memory usage, compute efficiency, and long-context handling. The models demonstrate significant performance gains across STEM, multimodal, and long-context benchmarks, competing with larger, state-of-the-art open models in human-rated tasks.

item.title: Researchers propose Multi-Mask Diffusion Model to improve few-step language generation by preserving masking structure and enabling drafting capability [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers introduce the Multi-Mask Diffusion Model (MultiMDM) to address challenges in few-step generation with masked diffusion models (MDMs), which typically collapse to a fully masked state and lack terminal entropy for consistency. MultiMDM pushes each clean token toward a designated mask in the forward process, allowing the backward process to predict masks before refining tokens, enhancing generation quality and efficiency. The team derives a closed-form ELBO training objective for MultiMDM that supports continual training from pretrained MDMs and develops a discrete-state consistency distillation scheme using shared-Gumbel coupling to reduce entropy. Experiments on pretraining and distillation demonstrate that MultiMDM provides an effective foundation for principled few-step language generation.

item.title: Researchers introduce RegretBench, a multi-turn benchmark evaluating LLMs' clarification policies using a regret-based objective to measure efficiency and effectiveness in ambiguous user interactions [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed RegretBench, a benchmark designed to assess how large language models (LLMs) handle clarification in conversations involving ambiguous user requests. Unlike traditional evaluations focusing on isolated question quality, RegretBench treats clarification as a sequential decision-making process, measuring how much value a model loses compared to a reference policy through a regret-based objective. The benchmark supports free-form interaction with semantic-state tracking and a hidden-intent formulation of ambiguity. Experiments using open-domain question answering and product recommendation scenarios demonstrate that models with similar accuracy can vary significantly in efficiency, robustness to user behavior, and decisions about when to stop clarifying. RegretBench jointly measures intent resolution, interaction cost, ineffective clarification, and regret to reveal whether models clarify usefully and efficiently. The findings indicate that effective clarification requires models to ask the right questions at the right time and to stop once the user's intended meaning is clear, rather than merely generating plausible questions.

item.title: Researchers identify Entropy-Gradient Inversion as a key internal mechanism in Large Reasoning Models and propose Correlation-Regularized Group Policy Optimization to improve reasoning performance [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have identified Entropy-Gradient Inversion, a negative correlation between token entropy and logit gradients, as a geometric fingerprint of reasoning capability in Large Reasoning Models (LRMs). They propose Correlation-Regularized Group Policy Optimization (CorR-PO), which incorporates this inversion into reinforcement learning reward regularization to enhance reasoning. Extensive experiments across multiple reasoning benchmarks and model scales demonstrate that CorR-PO consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, confirming that stronger Entropy-Gradient Inversion correlates with improved reasoning performance. This work addresses the gap between token-level behavior and internal reasoning mechanisms, as well as the instability of reinforcement learning methods relying on external verifiers.

item.title: Researchers dissociate factual and opinion sycophancy representations in large language models to improve interventions reducing sycophantic behavior [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Large Language Models (LLMs) often exhibit sycophancy by agreeing with users even when statements are incorrect. Researchers investigated whether different types of sycophancy-factual and opinion-based-are represented distinctly within LLMs' internal mechanisms. They trained probes and constructed steering vectors on one subtype's activations to test transferability to the other, revealing that LLMs vary in how aligned or distinct these representations are. The study used Linear Discriminant Analysis to visualize these differences and applied the findings to enhance methods for reducing sycophantic responses. This dissociation approach provides a general framework for analyzing the representational structure of complex behaviors in language models, potentially aiding future efforts to improve model reliability and alignment.

item.title: Researchers introduce Looped Latent Attention to compress K/V caches in looped Transformers, achieving up to 32× compression with near-lossless performance [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers present Looped Latent Attention (LLA), a post-training cache compression method for looped, weight-tied Transformers that reduces the memory footprint of key/value (K/V) caches by storing compact latent representations and reconstructing loop-specific vectors on demand. The approach leverages the low-rank structure of recurrent K/V caches and uses singular value decomposition (SVD) initialization refined through distillation techniques to achieve significant compression without loss of accuracy. LLA outperforms existing methods such as multi-head latent attention, cross-layer sharing, and quantization across models including Ouro-2.6B-Thinking and Huginn-3.5B, enabling exact cache reduction and increasing batch capacity by over 20 times on hardware like the H200. Additionally, on long reasoning tasks like MATH-500, on-policy refinement with LLA improves accuracy and reduces no-answer rates compared to token-level distillation, demonstrating practical benefits for efficient Transformer decoding.

item.title: Researchers introduce Staleness-Adaptive Trust Regions to stabilize asynchronous reinforcement learning by adjusting PPO clipping based on rollout staleness [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers propose the Staleness-Adaptive Trust Region (SAT) method to address instability in asynchronous reinforcement learning caused by stale rollouts from policy lag and system delays. SAT uses a staleness proxy to adaptively scale trust regions, making updates more conservative where staleness is high while preserving baseline behavior elsewhere. The approach was evaluated on a fully decoupled asynchronous setup using Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base with SGLang and Megatron, achieving improved performance metrics at various staleness lags. The results suggest that aligning PPO clipping intervals with observed staleness heterogeneity effectively stabilizes training in asynchronous reinforcement learning environments.

item.title: Researchers introduce Hybrid Hindsight Self-Distillation (H2SD) to improve reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards by adapting teacher context and update strategy based on trajectory correctness [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Hybrid Hindsight Self-Distillation (H2SD) addresses limitations in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) by providing different forms of hindsight supervision for successful and failed reasoning trajectories in language models. For successful trajectories, H2SD uses the verified response as privileged context to refine token credit assignment without altering reward direction, while for failed trajectories, it applies corrective guidance through reverse-KL distillation using verified reference hints. Experiments on challenging reasoning benchmarks demonstrate that H2SD outperforms representative RLVR and self-distillation baselines, offering stable optimization and a favorable balance between accuracy and efficiency.

item.title: Researchers find leftward ideological drift in hallucinations from large language models answering US political news questions [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers analyzed 21,727 expert-labeled US political news articles from left, center, and right sources to study hallucinations-unsupported statements-in large language model (LLM) question answering. They found that while hallucination rates vary by model and topic, the content of hallucinations consistently drifts leftward, even when generated from right-leaning sources. The study used a stance classifier and logit-level analysis to link hallucinations to high uncertainty in model outputs, suggesting an "uncertainty to guessing" mechanism. The team generated article-specific questions and elicited answers from three open-weight LLMs and one proprietary model, detecting hallucinations via reference comparison and classifying their ideological valence. Source ideology had modest impact on hallucination frequency, but hallucination content showed robust left-leaning bias. The findings have implications for auditing AI-mediated political information and designing safeguards for election-related deployments.

item.title: GaugeQuant introduces online learning of quantization-optimal bases using LLM symmetries to reduce activation outliers and improve perplexity in LLaMA-2 7B quantization [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: GaugeQuant is a method that leverages internal continuous symmetries in transformers during training by adding a LogSumExp term to the loss function, which breaks these symmetries and selects a basis minimizing activation outliers. It updates only rotation matrices via a stop-gradient operator, keeping the language modeling objective unchanged, and requires no calibration data or quantization simulation while adding minimal training overhead. Applied to the LLaMA-2 7B model with W4A4 quantization and group size 128, GaugeQuant reduces perplexity from 8.22 to 6.73, matching post-training methods that need frozen models and calibration datasets; under W4A16 quantization, perplexity drops from 11.16 to 5.45. The code is publicly available on GitHub.

item.title: Researchers evaluate open-weight large language models for AI-assisted longitudinal data preparation tasks on consumer-grade hardware [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers introduced an open-source framework to evaluate AI agents powered by open-weight large language models (LLMs) for data preparation in longitudinal population studies, addressing governance restrictions on sending sensitive data to cloud services. The framework includes a curated dataset, task definitions, and automated evaluation routines for R code and output data, focusing on tasks like category harmonization and multi-wave merging. The study benchmarks LLMs across consumer-grade deployments on 20 data preparation tasks involving 102 variables, finding that state-of-the-art 31-35 billion parameter models achieved up to 87.9% average task completion. The results suggest that open-weight LLMs running locally could enable AI-assisted data preparation in research settings with strict data governance. The framework is publicly available on GitHub.

item.title: OpenForgeRL launches open-source framework to train harness-native AI agents end-to-end across diverse environments at scale [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenForgeRL is an open-source framework designed to train AI agents that use complex inference harnesses like Claude Code, Codex, and OpenClaw in various environments. It uses a lightweight proxy to record model calls as training data and a Kubernetes orchestrator to run rollouts in remote containers, enabling scalable training on any harness. The framework supports training across tool-based and multimodal GUI agents, achieving strong benchmark results with relatively few tasks and outperforming similar-sized open baselines. Analysis shows that different harnesses vary in learning difficulty and that reinforcement learning improves agent reliability in tasks like self-verification and multi-step planning, though challenges remain in error recovery.

item.title: Researchers propose Spectral Flow Certificates to predict long-range propagation limits in Graph Neural Networks without training [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers introduce Spectral Flow Certificates (SFCs), a scalar metric computed from graph Laplacians that predicts whether Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) can effectively propagate information over long distances in a graph without requiring model training or labeled data. SFCs combine algebraic connectivity with message-passing depth to measure spectral bottlenecks, adapting dynamically as network depth changes and outperforming traditional graph statistics in explaining GNN accuracy on long-range tasks. The study evaluates SFCs across 25 synthetic graph families and 150 real molecular graphs from benchmark datasets, demonstrating over 90% explanatory power in predicting trained GNN accuracy before any training occurs. These findings suggest that a single eigenvalue computation can serve as an efficient preliminary filter to identify graphs where GNN training may be limited by topology, potentially saving computational resources in deployment scenarios.

item.title: SCOPE and SCION: A Benchmark and an Auditable Reference Pipeline for Schema Induction and Fusion from Text [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.21610v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Schema graphs are an upstream bottleneck of schema-grounded information extraction and knowledge graph construction, yet most extraction systems assume the schema is already available. We introduce SCOPE (Schema Construction and Ontology-induction Pipeline Evaluation), a train-text-only benchmark for corpus-to-schema induction and optional schema fusion from raw text, built from 24 public information extraction sources (15 RE and 9 EE) normalized into evaluation-only gold schema graphs; its core event-extraction target covers event types and within-event argument roles, with inter-event links reported separately. We present SCION (Schema Construction and Induction with Ontology Normalization), an auditable reference pipeline rather than a new extraction architecture; it constructs candidate spaces from train text and restricts naming, merging, filtering, validation, and conservative fusion to candidate-linked evidence under strict JSON contracts. On the SCOPE core suite, SCION-lite attains the highest F1 among released source-schema references, Text2Onto-style, LLM-only, and matched extract-then-aggregate baselines under Literal, Fuzzy, Continuous, and Graph schema-graph metrics, while the compact open-model SCION-RL variant reduces reliance on proprietary LLM schema engineers. These results are reported against normalized typed-edge targets rather than as claims that induced schemas surpass human ontology design; the release includes evidence-linked outputs, parse/fallback logs, candidate retention/merging logs, run manifests, code, and benchmark packages at https://github.com/wandugu/paper_scion.

item.title: Procedural Knowledge Is Not Low-Rank: Why LoRA Fails to Internalize Multi-Step Procedures [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.21612v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods like LoRA have become the default for adapting large language models, succeeding across instruction following, style transfer, and factual adaptation. We show that for procedural knowledge--the ability to follow multi-step procedures with conditional branching through to terminal states--LoRA fails to match full fine-tuning at the ranks where it retains its efficiency advantage. In a systematic ablation (r = 16--128) on a procedural travel booking task (14 nodes), all LoRA configurations fail uniformly (task success <= 2.54 vs. 4.11 for full fine-tuning, all p < 0.001), with scores decreasing at higher ranks--despite maintaining 95--99% conversation completion rates. Cross-domain replication on Zoom support (14 nodes) and insurance claims (55 nodes) at 8B confirms the failure generalizes: LoRA underperforms full fine-tuning by 0.8--2.2 points on average at both r = 32 and r = 128, with the largest gap on the most complex procedure. Quadrupling rank from 32 to 128 provides marginal improvement but does not close the gap. SVD analysis of the weight changes produced by full fine-tuning explains why: across three domains at both 3B and 8B, the mean effective rank of the update ranges from 761 to 1,026, and rank 128 captures only 43--51% of the squared Frobenius norm. Together, these findings establish that for procedural tasks LoRA falls well short of full fine-tuning--a fundamental limitation for agentic applications.

item.title: FrED: External Data Influence Estimation via Domain Knowledge Graph Grounding [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.21615v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The rapid deployment of generative AI has amplified the critical need for Training Data Attribution to ensure transparency and accountability. However, current parametric approaches require computationally prohibitive access to model weights, while similarity-based methods ignore deep structural context. We propose a novel probabilistic framework that operates entirely in a black-box setting. Our method fuses continuous feature similarities with discrete, domain-specific Knowledge Graphs (KGs). This approach ensures the attribution is grounded in structural reality, explicitly rewarding highly specific historical samples while preventing generic background data from dominating the results. We evaluate our framework across two distinct domains where linking outputs to data and domain context is inherently complex: abstract artistic image synthesis and high-dimensional physical weather forecasting. Extensive benchmarking demonstrates the robust efficacy of our approach. In the artistic domain, it achieves a strong Linear Datamodeling Score that exceeds standard black-box similarity baselines, while closing much of the gap to gradient-based estimators. We additionally present a cross-domain feasibility case study in environmental forecasting, where we use domain KGs to retrieve physically consistent historical analogs for regional flood forecasts, improving geographic localisation over a latent-only baseline. Operating entirely without internal model access, our approach provides an efficient, interpretable mechanism for post-hoc influence analysis and domain-grounded retrieval.

item.title: FBLayout: Optimizing Memory Layout for Efficient LLM Finetuning on Mobile GPUs [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.21624v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transformer-based models have enabled unprecedented capabilities across language, vision, and multimodal tasks. On-device fine-tuning of transformer models offers a privacy-preserving path to personalized AI, yet remains inefficient on mobile GPUs due to severe memory constraints and frequent layout transformations in attention mechanism during training. Existing mobile training frameworks either use unified layouts for forward and backward passes -- leading to fragmented memory access and poor GPU utilization during backpropagation -- or rely on explicit layout conversions, which introduce significant transformation overhead. To overcome this, we propose FBLayout, a layout-aware framework that co-designs tensor organization with mobile GPU platforms. FBLayout introduces: (1) a unified R-Tile layout for multi-dimensional reductions across forward/backward passes; (2) tile-based index transformation to eliminate physical data movement; and (3) activation-guided layout selection to propagate efficient layouts globally. Evaluations on seven transformer models across different mobile phones (including ARM Mali and Qualcomm Adreno GPUs) show that FBLayout achieves 2.2-5.7x speedup over MNN, TFLite, and TVM, while significantly improving cache efficiency and reducing memory footprint, enabling practical on-device large model fine-tuning.

item.title: Do Modules Stay in Their Lane? Role Drift in Compound LLM Systems [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.21627v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: End-to-end reinforcement learning can improve the accuracy of compound LLM systems, but it does not constrain how modules divide labor internally. We identify Role Drift, a failure mode in which modules preserve or improve end-task performance while deviating from their assigned roles through role-violating shortcuts that remain invisible to system-level evaluation. To make role drift observable and controllable, we propose Role Anchor, a regularizer that modulates how much each module deviates from its assigned role during end-to-end training. The key idea is to preserve how the role prompt shifts the module's next-token predictions relative to a neutral prompt, which serves as a proxy for the role's intended effect during training. Experiments on two compound LLM pipelines reveal role drift that accuracy alone fails to detect: a decomposer meant to split a question into sub-questions for a separate solver instead plants the answer in them, and a reader meant to answer from retrieved passages instead falls back on parametric memory. In fact, on the decomposer pipeline this shortcut drives most of the apparent RL gain: 86% of it vanishes once the decomposer is held to its role, indicating that terminal accuracy alone can badly overstate how much a compound system has genuinely learned. Across both pipelines, Role Anchor mitigates role drift at a tunable accuracy cost that varies by pipeline and anchor strength. Additional gradient analysis suggests that the regularizer reduces alignment with the role-drift direction rather than simply suppressing learning.

item.title: Reasoning Denoiser: Denoising Reasoning Traces for Hallucination Detection in Large Reasoning Models [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.22098v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large reasoning models (LRMs) generate long reasoning traces before producing final answers. While these traces may contain useful signals for hallucination detection, harnessing them is non-trivial because long trajectories often include noisy steps that obscure the cues relevant to truthfulness assessment. In this paper, we identify two prevalent forms of reasoning noises, i.e., irrelevant steps and repetitive steps, and show that both substantially degrade hallucination detection performance. Existing confidence-based scores and naive embedding-based filtering fail to reliably separate noisy from informative steps. To address this challenge, we propose REDE, a novel learning framework for denoising reasoning traces for hallucination detection. Specifically, REDE leverages final-answer attention as an automatic supervision signal to shape the step-level representation space, yielding refined embeddings in which noisy steps can be reliably identified and filtered. REDE can be readily plugged into diverse hallucination detectors by operating on the filtered reasoning trajectory after removing noisy steps. Extensive experiments on multiple reasoning benchmarks show that REDE consistently improves detection performance over competitive baselines.

item.title: Industrial Tokenization for LLM-Based Health Intelligence: A Federated Architecture for Industrial Evidence Integration [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.22153v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Industrial health management increasingly relies on heterogeneous information sources, including condition monitoring systems, supervisory control and data acquisition systems, maintenance records, inspection results, and prognostic models. Although large language models provide new opportunities for cross-source reasoning, industrial data and analytical outputs differ substantially in structure, temporal resolution, physical meaning, and reliability. Directly integrating such heterogeneous information into a monolithic model may reduce interpretability, traceability, and adaptability to equipment and data changes. This paper introduces Industrial Tokenization, a conceptual interface for transforming source-specific analytical outputs into structured and machine-interpretable units of industrial evidence, termed Industrial Tokens. Unlike numerical tokens used to encode raw time-series data, Industrial Tokens represent domain-grounded evidence together with source, temporal scope, operating context, analytical meaning, quality or confidence information, and provenance. Based on this concept, a federated industrial architecture is proposed, where heterogeneous analytical subsystems retain autonomy while exposing standardized Industrial Tokens to a central reasoning layer. As an initial implementation, this study presents an end-to-end DiagnosisToken pathway based on vibration-diagnostic outputs, rule-based event aggregation, structured textual token generation, and LLM-based interpretation. Other Industrial Tokens, including SCADA-based condition-monitoring tokens, maintenance tokens, and prognostic tokens, are reserved as future extensions. The proposed framework positions Industrial Tokenization as a semantic interface between domain-specific industrial intelligence and LLM- or agent-based reasoning, rather than another method for encoding raw industrial data.

item.title: Agentic Root Cause Analysis through Evidence-Grounded Reasoning [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.22385v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Diagnosing the root cause of anomalies is essential for safe industrial operation. Despite extensive sensor instrumentation, formulating hypotheses and gathering evidence remains a manual process, creating a major operational bottleneck. While existing data-driven approaches aim to automate this, two critical limitations restrict their deployment: their operate as black boxes unable to justify their diagnosis, and they require scarce labeled examples of faulty operation. To address this gap, we introduce AgentRCA, a zero-shot agentic framework for evidence-grounded root cause analysis. Rather than learning fault-specific mappings, AgentRCA performs inference-time reasoning by combining a data-driven digital twin (modeling normal system dynamics) with a tool-augmented large language model. The agent iteratively gathers statistical evidence, evaluates competing hypotheses, and identifies the physical fault that best explains the observed behavior. Evaluated on a real-world multiphase-flow facility and a large-scale chemical plant, AgentRCA achieves diagnostic performance competitive with fully supervised baselines without relying on fault-specific training. Crucially, it produces transparent reasoning traces that explicitly link observed symptoms to their underlying physical causes. These results establish autonomous hypothesis-driven reasoning as a practical foundation for scalable industrial root cause analysis.

item.title: TRACE-ROUTER: Task-Consistent and Adaptive Online Routing for Agentic AI [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.22465v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Routing to select large language models (LLMs) with different cost-quality trade-offs has become a fundamental deployment feature of enterprise AI. Existing routers, primarily make independent routing decisions for each LLM call. However, agentic applications execute as long-horizon workflows whose quality is determined only by a delayed, task-level outcome. This mismatch prevents per-call routers from correctly attributing feedback to individual routing decisions. Towards mitigating this, we present TRACE-Router, a task-level routing framework that aligns routing with the unit of supervision. TRACE-Router assigns each task to a model once at admission using a contextual bandit, pins all subsequent LLM calls to the selected backend, and updates its policy using the task's terminal reward, jointly accounting for accuracy and latency. By leveraging delayed task feedback, TRACE-Router learns routing policies that adapt to the workload while avoiding explicit task-complexity estimation. Across three agentic benchmarks, TRACE-Router consistently improves the accuracy-latency trade-off, achieving non-dominated Pareto frontier points. On tau2-Bench, it outperforms latency-matched interpolation between individual models by 7-8 accuracy points, while on Terminal-Bench it achieves 7.1 higher accuracy points than the strongest single model baseline with 36% lower latency.

item.title: Do emulated quantum circuits change what CNNs look at? Performance and explainability comparison in medical image classification [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.21186v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Numerous studies have analyzed the use of hybrid quantum-classical convolutional neural networks as a promising alternative to classical deep learning. However, network components on quantum hardware impose fundamental limitations, while the scalability of quantum circuits leads to trainability issues. In this work, we investigate whether small, classically-emulated quantum circuit components can play a meaningful role within complex models, offering an alternative to purely classical convolutional architectures. To this end, we present a systematic study of the effectiveness of a Hybrid Quantum-inspired Convolutional Neural Network (HQiCNN) compared with a parameter-matched classical Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) that differs only in an intermediate dense neural layer. Both models are evaluated on two real-world medical datasets while systematically varying the different hyperparameters, ensuring a fair model comparison that is both dataset and hyperparameter independent. The results show that no architecture consistently dominates the other: the HQiCNN achieves its largest gains in intermediate-data regimes, whereas the CNN reaches the highest accuracies for the largest training sets in both datasets. Furthermore, removing entanglement produces comparable performance while enabling substantially better scalability of quantum simulations, and richer observable sets become beneficial only when sufficient training data are available. Finally, we propose two SHAP-based explainability tools for comparing the predictions between both models, $|SHAP|$IoU and $EMD_{pos}$ metric, to demonstrate that both architectures consistently attend to anatomically plausible regions. Thus, we provide a comprehensive benchmark showing that, under certain conditions, hybrid quantum-inspired models are an alternative that can offer benefits in practical tasks such as medical image classification.

item.title: Local Synaptic Rules Can Implement a SIGReg Gradient Without Backpropagation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.21622v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that two canonical local synaptic learning rules, the potentiation arm of spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP$^+$) and homeostatic plasticity (instantiated here via flashlight granule-cell-like neurons), together can implement the exact gradient of a SIGReg-like self-supervised learning objective. The equivalence requires no gradient calculations, no global error signals, no weight transport, and no label information: the only inputs are pre- and post-synaptic firing rates, local firing statistics, and the temporal contiguity of natural sensory streams. On a synthetic clustering task designed to probe whether class structure can be recovered from temporal ordering of inputs alone, ordered presentation raised cluster separation (CSR) to 2.49 while random ordering left it near baseline (0.83), a roughly threefold ($\approx 3.5\sigma$) separation attributable solely to input ordering. On temporally ordered MNIST, a two-layer network trained entirely with these rules achieved 87.3% linear-probe accuracy, showing that the mechanism functions end-to-end.

item.title: On the Depth Scalability of Logic Gate Networks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.21633v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Logic Gate Networks (LGNs) implement computation through compositions of Boolean operations, yet unlike classical Boolean circuits, existing LGNs do not reliably benefit from increased depth. We identify two distinct causes: optimization collapse in deep relaxed LGNs and a topology-induced limitation that persists even when skip-biased initialization and straight-through estimation stabilize training. Thus, trainability alone is insufficient; deeper layers must also receive information that supports useful computation. We introduce Input-Anchored Logic Gate Networks (IALGNs), in which each gate combines an evolving hidden feature with a direct input anchor. This topology preserves a computational spine while conditioning every layer on the original input. We show that a depth-D path can depend on up to D+1 input bits and establish a strict path-wise depth hierarchy. Random-k anchor relaxation further improves anchor selection without relaxing the spine. Across MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100, IALGNs achieve consistent fixed-width depth--accuracy improvements beyond 100 layers, whereas alternative LGN topologies saturate or degrade. Layer-wise probes, topology ablations, and effective-depth analysis show that input anchoring produces progressively more informative representations and preserves longer computational paths. These results demonstrate that scalable depth in LGNs requires both stable optimization and an information-access pattern that supports input-conditioned refinement.

item.title: MotifRole-Diff: Risk-Optimal Role-Aware Corruption for Masked Molecular Graph Diffusion [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.21634v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Masked discrete diffusion for molecular graph generation typically applies a uniform corruption schedule to all tokens in a lossless graph-to-sequence representation, implicitly treating structurally heterogeneous molecular components as equally difficult and equally important to reconstruct. However, different molecular graph token roles exhibit substantial variation in denoising difficulty and their influence on the decoded molecule, motivating role-specific corruption strategies. We introduce MotifRole-Diff, a role-aware corruption process that allocates masking rates according to empirically measured denoising difficulty and graph-level perturbation impact while preserving the model architecture, clean sequence space, and lossless molecular-graph decoder. We formulate schedule selection as the risk-optimal allocation of a fixed masking budget across token roles. Our theorem characterizes optimality for the modeled role-weighted residual risk, while downstream generation performance is evaluated empirically. Under matched architecture, training budget, and sampling compute, MotifRole-Diff improves validity on QM9 from 0.905 to 0.944 while reducing FCD from 1.701 to 1.609, and on MOSES improves validity from 0.920 to 0.938 while reducing FCD from 2.125 to 1.850. Role-wise diagnostics further show improved reconstruction across molecular graph token categories. Together, these matched-compute results indicate that structurally informed corruption is a more effective masking strategy than uniform schedules for serialized molecular graph diffusion.

item.title: Measuring the Dependency Gap: Diagnosing Inter-Column Fidelity in Tabular Generative Models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.21636v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Synthetic tabular data is valued for preserving not only each column's marginal distribution but the dependencies between columns -- structure that carries much of the discriminative signal for minority classes in imbalanced domains such as fraud and clinical risk. Yet the metrics most commonly used to certify synthetic tabular data are, we show, largely blind to inter-column dependency: a baseline that models every column independently (and therefore destroys all dependency) is judged indistinguishable from real data by the logistic-regression C2ST, and the pairwise Trend score is only partially sensitive. We introduce a dependency-aware fidelity diagnostic that decomposes a strong classifier two-sample test (XGB-C2ST) into marginal, dependency, and numerical-categorical cross components, anchored between a worst-case fully-factorized reference (all dependency destroyed) and a best-case real-data oracle. Applying it to a state-of-the-art flow-matching generator (TabbyFlow/EF-VFM), we find a real dependency gap that standard metrics miss; destroying dependency outright collapses minority-class utility, and the generator's residual gap carries a smaller, consistent utility cost. We then ask whether this gap reflects a structural limitation of mean-field generative objectives. It does not: consistent with recent recovery results for variational flow matching, the objective is asymptotically exact. Yet the gap is stubborn -- a 16x increase in model capacity does not close it -- pointing to the absence of direct dependency supervision rather than a capacity or structural limit. Consistent with this, and because the residual gap is higher-order, no cheap intervention closes it: not an in-model dependency mechanism, not post-hoc copula correction, and not the 16x capacity increase -- a caution for a field that assumes such fixes help.

item.title: Multi-Horizon Consistency as Geometry: When Latent Dynamics Contract, and When They Do Not [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.21645v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-horizon latent consistency is a common training knob in video predictors and world models, but practitioners rarely know what it does to transition geometry. We treat lambda, the weight on multi-step latent agreement, as a diagnostic control and measure an empirical expansion proxy L20,q95 together with horizon-20 prediction error E20. On Moving-MNIST (n=6 seeds at the critical pair), raising lambda from 0 to 0.8 cuts L20 from 4.96 +/- 2.01 to 1.01 +/- 0.06 (paired t p=0.005, Wilcoxon p=0.031) and halves E20 (0.365 to 0.177, paired t p=1.1e-13). Four of six seeds cross L<1 at lambda=0.8. The same loss does not produce population L<1 on action-conditioned Pendulum-v1 or CartPole-v1, nor on KTH Actions video, even when E20 improves. An associational mediation analysis on MMNIST gives r-hat=0.94 (95% CI [0.88, 1.00], n=27, B=2000); lambda was not randomized. Defensive checks (architectural baselines, exogenous stress, WorldTest, MPC, scaling) mostly support a narrow claim: soft consistency can push passive video toward a near-contractive band, and that band is domain-limited. A stochastic-forcing law L20 ~ 1.23 + 1.82 eta at lambda=0.8 (bootstrap slope CI [1.73, 1.92], R^2=0.96) unifies control domains on the same curve via calibrated eta_eff. Complete joint slices at lambda in {0.4, 1.2} (30/30 cells, 5 eta x 3 seeds) show comparable linear L20(eta) slopes (~1.69 and ~2.00); we do not fit a continuous (lambda, eta) surface. We do not report DreamerV3 or TD-MPC2 returns.

item.title: A Drift Stable Quantum Federated Learning for Intelligent Services [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.21647v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum federated learning enables distributed clients to train quantum neural networks without sharing local data, making it promising for privacy-aware intelligent services. Intelligent services in this context refer to privacy-sensitive distributed decision systems, such as fraud detection and genomic classification, where reliable and fair client-level learning is as important as the accuracy of the aggregate model. However, heterogeneous client data and noisy quantum optimization often cause unstable local updates, client drift, and unfair performance between clients. This paper proposes DUQFL-Prox, a drift-stable quantum federated learning framework based on deep-unfolded local optimization. Instead of using a fixed local optimizer, each client performs adaptive unfolded SPSA updates, while a proximal term keeps the local model close to the global model. A lightweight controller learns step-specific optimization parameters to improve post-aggregation performance. Experiments on financial fraud and genomic classification tasks show that DUQFL-Prox improves stability, generalization, and client fairness compared with standard QFL baselines. The results suggest that deep-unfolded quantum federated learning can support more reliable and fair intelligent services in heterogeneous distributed environments.

item.title: Generative and multimodal AI for materials prediction and design: Progress, challenges, and perspectives [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.21660v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is accelerating materials prediction and design by enabling efficient exploration of chemical and structural spaces, with particular promise for novel materials discovery. However, novelty in materials discovery encompasses chemical plausibility, structural distinctiveness, property relevance and experimental realisability, making AI-driven novelty claims difficult to substantiate. We introduce a materials property hierarchy, from intrinsic, composition-determined properties to extrinsic, processing-dependent performance, to clarify deployment constraints and distinguish structural, physical and deployment novelty. This framework motivates an evidence-based view of multimodal materials data spanning chemical composition, microstructure, processing, and testing and characterisation, showing that current evidence remains concentrated in composition and idealised structure while heterogeneous, under-represented and weakly integrated modalities limit support for physical and deployment novelty. It also highlights the limitations of benchmarks based mainly on computational labels and proxy novelty criteria. Community-wide standards for data collection, modality alignment and evidence synthesis are needed to support multimodal data construction, process-aware multimodal modelling, feasibility-first generative modelling and deployment-aware benchmarking, so that generative and multimodal AI can design experimentally realisable materials with defensible scientific and practical novelty.
